name: creative-clippath

frames.best_why: All three carved-out shapes are fully visible in a clean row, showing the squiggly silhouettes clearly.

tagline: Three photos clipped into lumpy organic shapes in a row.
summary: A three-column strip where each media item is cut out with a hand-drawn squiggly silhouette: a red-toned camera portrait, a broccoli clip on deep blue, and a pale tower-and-camera shot.
appearance: Three tall media panels sit side by side on a white card. Each is clipped to a different lumpy, scalloped outline rather than a rectangle: left a red-toned photo of hands and a vintage camera, middle a bright broccoli head on deep blue, right a pale sepia building scene with a camera.
behaviour: The middle panel is a looping video whose leaves shimmer slightly. Pointing at any panel scales its content up a little within the fixed cut-out silhouette, so the picture grows but the shape stays put.
demo_content: A vintage camera in hands, a broccoli head on blue, and a pale tower scene.
use_when: A portfolio or brand page wants a playful break from rectangular image grids.
avoid_when: The demo pulls photos and a video from external URLs, and the crop can cut off subjects at small sizes.
customise: The three media URLs, their clip-path definitions and alt text are hardcoded; swapping images means editing the file and matching each figure to a shape id.
weight_why: Two images plus an always-playing background video; light DOM but decoding video costs.

a11y.note: Both photos use the alt text 'Description', the video has no label or captions, and the autoplay loop ignores prefers-reduced-motion.

issues: Both images share the alt text 'Description'.
The autoplaying video gives no captions or motion control.
polish_why: Striking organic cut-outs and vivid colours; generic alt text and uncontrolled autoplay detract.
title: Creative Squiggle Clip Path
